title: Platform Tutorial Review
description: Test your understanding of how to use the learning platform.

questions.question: What are the three phases of this Python course?
options: Intro, Middle, and Final Exam
Fundamentals, Intermediate, and Advanced Projects
HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
Python Basics and 50 different games
questions.explanation: The course is structured into Phase 1 (Fundamentals), Phase 2 (Intermediate), and Phase 3 (Advanced Projects) to guide you from beginner to advanced level.

questions.question: What can you do on this learning platform?
options: Only read lessons and watch videos
Write, run, and test Python code in your browser
Download Python programs to run on your computer
Only take quizzes and tests
questions.explanation: This is an interactive platform where you can write Python code directly in your browser, run it instantly, and get immediate feedback on your solutions.

questions.question: What will you earn as you progress through the course?
options: Only a certificate at the end
XP points and badges for completing lessons
Money for each module completed
Nothing - it's just for learning
questions.explanation: The platform uses gamification to motivate learning. You'll earn XP (experience points) for completing lessons and unlock badges for achievements.

questions.question: What is the primary benefit of Syntax Highlighting?
options: It automatically fixes your code for you
It uses different colors to help you spot errors and understand code structure
It makes the code run faster in the terminal
It translates Python into other languages
questions.explanation: Syntax Highlighting color-codes different parts of your code (like strings, comments, and keywords). This makes it easier to read and helps you notice if you've made a typo when the colors don't look right.

questions.question: Where should you look to find the specific tasks you need to complete for an exercise?
options: In the terminal output
The Exercise Instructions at the top of the editor
Inside the Code Folding menu
In the Python documentation website
questions.explanation: The 'Exercise Instructions' (labeled as point 2 in our layout) tell you exactly what you need to code to pass the lesson and earn your XP.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the Python Terminal on this platform?
options: To write and save long programs for later
To see the output of your code and test small snippets interactively
To change the background color of the website
To download the Python 'Engine' to your computer
questions.explanation: The terminal is the 'output window' where your code comes to life. It shows you the results of your programs and allows for quick, interactive testing.

questions.question: If you see a 'SyntaxError' in the terminal output, what does it usually mean?
options: Your internet connection was lost
The terminal is full and needs to be cleared
There is a mistake in the way your code is written (like a missing quote)
The code ran perfectly
questions.explanation: A SyntaxError means Python didn't understand your instructions because they didn't follow the language rules—like a typo or a missing bracket.

questions.question: Which button would you use if the terminal becomes cluttered and you want a fresh start?
options: The Run button
The Download button
The Clear Terminal (trash can) button
The Show Hints button
questions.explanation: The Clear Terminal button (point 5 in our layout) wipes the output area clean so you can see your next code execution more clearly.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between 'Run Code' and 'Submit Code'?
options: Run Code is for practicing/testing, while Submit Code checks for correctness and awards XP
Run Code is for Python, while Submit Code is for other languages
Submit Code is only used for downloading files
There is no difference; they perform the same action
questions.explanation: The 'Run' button allows you to test your code as many times as you like in the terminal. The 'Submit' button is the final step to validate your solution against requirements and earn your progress.

questions.question: In what order does Python execute the lines of code you write in the editor?
options: It runs all lines at the exact same time
It starts from the bottom and works its way up
From top to bottom, one line at a time
It only runs the lines that contain numbers
questions.explanation: Python is a sequential language; it follows your instructions in order from the first line down to the last. This is why you must define variables before you use them!

questions.question: How is the entire Python course organized?
options: In one long list of 100 lessons
Into 3 Phases containing a total of 20 Modules
By random topics that change every week
By alphabetical order only
questions.explanation: The course is structured into 3 logical Phases (Fundamentals, Intermediate, and Projects) to help you build your skills step-by-step.

questions.question: What is the purpose of 'Review Mode'?
options: To delete your progress and start over
To revisit a completed lesson and practice exercises without affecting your XP
To skip a lesson you find too difficult
To change the website's theme
questions.explanation: Review Mode allows you to go back and strengthen your skills on topics you've already passed without worrying about your official progress score.

questions.question: What does the 'Download' button on a lesson allow you to do?
options: It prints a physical copy of the lesson
It saves your current code to your computer so you can use it in your own IDE
It downloads a video of the lesson instructor
It clears all the code you have written
questions.explanation: The download button lets you take the Python code files from the platform and save them locally. This allows you to practice using your own professional tools.

questions.question: Besides a code editor, what must be installed on your computer to run Python code locally?
options: A specialized gaming mouse
The Python 'Engine' (Interpreter) from python.org
A premium subscription to a cloud service
Nothing, computers understand Python automatically
questions.explanation: To run Python code on your computer, you must install the Python interpreter. Think of it as the 'engine' that translates your code into instructions the computer can follow.

questions.question: What is an IDE (Integrated Development Environment)?
options: A fast type of internet for developers
A special keyboard used for Python
Professional 'all-in-one' software for writing and testing code (like VS Code)
The part of the computer that stores your files
questions.explanation: An IDE like VS Code or PyCharm is a 'Dashboard' for developers. It combines a text editor with powerful tools like error detection and file management.
